There is a clear history of exposure to another affected child at daycare — a classic epidemiologic clue for molluscum contagiosum (MCV), a common, self-limited viral infection in young children. The absence of systemic symptoms, pruritus, or involvement of other body sites further supports a localized, benign viral etiology. While dermatoscopic and histopathologic features (e.g., umbilication, Henderson-Paterson bodies) are highly suggestive, they are not mandatory for diagnosis in typical cases.
